newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Capital Intelligence reduces USCB bank rating.
newsitem.headline: Capital Intelligence reduces USCB bank rating.

text.p: Capital Intelligence, the Cyprus-based specialist bank rating agency on Thursday said it has downgraded the long-term rating of United Saudi Commercial Bank (USCB) to A- from A.
USCB's short-term rating is reaffirmed at A-1 and a stable outlook has been assigned for the next 12 months, Capital Intelligence said in an announcement.
The long-term rating is downgraded to reflect the increase in overdue loans in 1995, the agency said.

Although this was a common phenomenon for Saudi banks last year, the extent of the increase at USCB and the corresponding fall in the provisioning coverage, excluding collateral, have been particularly steep, Capital Intelligence said.
It is likely the bank will need to raise provisioning levels for the current year.
A further disadvantage faced by USCB as a wholesale bank is its small branch network which limits expansion of its retail deposit base, Capital Intelligence said.

With total assets of $2.9 billion, USCB is Saudi Arabia's third smallest bank, maintaining a 3.2 percent market share of total banking assets. It operates through a local network of 17 branches. The bank's strategy stresses efficiency, superior customer service and operational automation, catering for an exclusive target market mostly comprising high net worth individials and private blue chip businesses.
Prince Al Waleed Bin Talal, the high- profile international financier and the bank's chairman, is believed to control 40 percent of the bank's capital, Capital Intelligence said.
